title: Justice
subtitle: The Splendor of the Great Song — Rebuilding the Craftsmanship of a Dynasty with Digital Technology
description: Justice is a massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed by Thunder Fire Studio under NetEase Games, set in the Northern Song dynasty. Based on the Along the River During the Qingming Festival's depiction of Bianliang, the game strives to recreate a freely explorable Northern Song eastern capital. More notably, the game launched the 'Great Song Architecture Restoration Project' — collaborating with the Palace Museum, the Henan Provincial Institute of Cultural Heritage and Archaeology, and other institutions to大量 collect survey and影像 data of Song dynasty heritage buildings, using digital technology to bring vanished or endangered Song structures back to life.

route.title: Justice: A Journey of Craftsmanship Along the Qingming Festival Scroll
route.intro:
The dreams of Dongjing — a thousand years in an instant
In the history of Chinese online games, no title has taken 'architecture' as a core selling point the way Justice has. When it launched in 2018, most players' first impression was not the combat feel or the story length, but — 'the Bianjing in this game is enormous!' Indeed, the Bianjing in the game is nearly a one-to-one reconstruction based on the textual records of Along the River During the Qingming Festival and Dongjing Menghua Lu: the Rainbow Bridge, the Bian River, Daxiangguo Temple, Kaibao Temple's Iron Pagoda, the Zhou Bridge night market... the Northern Song Dongjing, which had existed only in text and pictures, 'came alive' on screen for the first time. But even more worthy of respect is the subsequent 'Great Song Architecture Restoration Project.' The game team was not satisfied with merely 'looking the part' — they partnered with academic institutions including the Palace Museum to systematically digitally collect heritage sites such as Kaifeng's Youguo Temple Pagoda, Luoyang's Longmen Grottoes, Suzhou's Humble Administrator's Garden, and Yangzhou's Ge Garden. This has far surpassed a game's cultural responsibility — it is an unprecedented digital preservation project for Chinese ancient architecture.

stops.title: Stop 1: Bianjing Daxiangguo Temple — The Buddha's Grand Bazaar of Ten Thousand Traders
stops.content: The most central landmark in the game's Bianjing — and the social hub where players most often gather — is Daxiangguo Temple. In Justice, Daxiangguo Temple is reconstructed as a vast imperial monastery complex: a five-bay mountain gate with double-eaved hip roof, bell and drum towers facing each other on east and west; the Four Heavenly Kings in the Heavenly King Hall with glaring eyes; the Mahavira Hall nine bays wide and five bays deep, with double-eaved歇山顶 covered in yellow glazed tiles, a broad front platform spacious enough to accommodate hundreds of players practicing martial arts or setting up stalls. Historically, Daxiangguo Temple originally stood on the former residence of Lord Xinling of the Warring States period, converted to Jianguo Temple in the Northern Qi. Emperor Ruizong of Tang, Li Dan, bestowed the name 'Daxiangguo Temple' to commemorate his accession from the title of Prince of Xiang. In the Northern Song, Daxiangguo Temple was not only the national Buddhist center but also the largest commercial market in the eastern capital — five 'Ten Thousand Trader' markets each month, with merchants gathering from all directions, a bustling世俗 prosperity described vividly in Dongjing Menghua Lu. The game faithfully reproduces this奇妙 atmosphere of 'Buddha land coexisting with marketplace.' The square outside the temple is filled with player stalls — precisely the real daily life of Northern Song Daxiangguo Temple — while inside the hall, incense before the Buddha never ceases. In terms of architectural details, the pagoda spire of the game's Daxiangguo Temple references the glazed components of Kaifeng's Youguo Temple Pagoda. Youguo Temple Pagoda, i.e., the Kaifeng Iron Pagoda, was built in the first year of the Northern Song's Huangyou era (1049), thirteen stories on an octagonal plan, about 55 meters tall, its entire body built from brown glazed bricks, looking like cast iron from a distance. Every brick is impressed with exquisite patterns of Buddha figures, apsaras, musicians, and qilins — over nine hundred years, neither earthquake nor flood has dislodged it. The glazed pagoda on the east side of the game's monastery transplants the Iron Pagoda's 'brown glazed' language into the temple space. As you pass through the incense-filled Heavenly King Hall and emerge onto the platform to see the glittering array of player stalls — you are also seeing that morning in Dongjing, nine hundred years ago, when ten thousand people gathered together.

stops.title: Stop 2: Kaifeng Iron Pagoda — Nine Hundred Years of Unshakable Standing
stops.content: In Justice's Bianjing, no matter where you stand, when you look to the northeast, you will always see a towering brown-glazed pagoda — Youguo Temple Pagoda, the Kaifeng Iron Pagoda. Youguo Temple Pagoda (Kaifeng Iron Pagoda) is the oldest intact above-ground building in Kaifeng and the tallest and oldest glazed pagoda in China. Built in the first year of the Northern Song's Huangyou era (1049), it was originally part of Kaibao Temple. The pagoda has thirteen stories on an octagonal plan, about 55 meters tall, entirely built from brown glazed bricks, looking like cast iron from a distance — hence its popular name. In the game, the Iron Pagoda is placed on the original site of Kaibao Temple in the northeastern corner of Kaifeng — consistent with historical fact. Even more movingly, the game reproduces with高精度 textures the most exquisite details of the Iron Pagoda — the Buddha figures, apsaras, musicians, lions, qilins, and other patterns impressed into the glazed bricks. Players can walk to the foot of the pagoda and look up at these miniature carvings, just as if standing at the foot of this thousand-year-old pagoda in real life. The craft of these glazed bricks itself is a miracle in architectural history: each brick was first pressed in a mold to create the pattern, then glazed with brown glaze and fired at high temperature in a kiln. Over nine hundred years, Kaifeng has experienced dozens of Yellow River floods, the entire city buried under silt several times — only the Iron Pagoda, because each brick interlocks with mortise-and-tenon-like grooves, has remained unshakable through earthquakes and floods. The game reproduces this interlocking structure — if you examine the pagoda body closely, you can see the tiny凹凸 grooves on the edges of the glazed bricks; they are not decoration but the secret of the Iron Pagoda's thousand-year resilience. In the area where the Iron Pagoda stands, the game also restores the unique nature of the Song dynasty Kaibao Temple: it was a monastery that融合d Buddhism and technology — during the Northern Song, the temple housed the world's tallest wooden pagoda (the Linggan Wooden Pagoda), later destroyed by lightning fire. Around the Kaibao Temple pagoda in the game are scattered some mechanical devices with a scientific air — alluding to the Northern Song's时代 characteristic of 'valuing technology.' The most touching digital detail of the Iron Pagoda is that in the game, you can climb to the top of the thirteenth story. From a cinematic perspective, the entire Bianjing city spreads out beneath you — the Rainbow Bridge, the Bian River, Xiangguo Temple, the Zhou Bridge — nine hundred years ago, standing here overlooking the Dongjing might have been a night watchman, or a poet gazing alone at the moon from the city wall.

stops.title: Stop 3: Hangzhou Leifeng Pagoda — The Buddha's Fading Shadow in West Lake's Mist and Rain
stops.content: Leaving Bianjing and sailing south, the player's next stop is another meticulously recreated city in Justice — Lin'an (Hangzhou). The Leifeng Pagoda by West Lake is one of the most stunning scenes in Justice. In the game, it is placed on Sunset Peak of Nanping Mountain. Every dusk, as the sun passes through the pagoda's delicate window openings, the light spills across the lake — this is 'Leifeng Sunset,' spoken of by countless people but rarely seen, and the game's graphics engine fulfills an eight-hundred-year-old dream. However, the historical Leifeng Pagoda (note: not the present one) was itself not a heritage site — it collapsed in 1924, and the current 'Leifeng Pagoda' was rebuilt on the original site in 2002. But the game is not content with merely recreating the Leifeng Pagoda's exterior. It integrates the surrounding architectural environment with other Hangzhou heritage buildings, creating the concept of a 'West Lake Architectural Culture Circle.' In the southern shore area where Leifeng Pagoda sits, the game absorbs the architectural vocabulary of many Hangzhou ancient buildings — white-walled, black-tiled folk houses built along the water, stone docks extending into the lake, distant pavilions and towers faintly visible. The architectural genes of these scenes can be traced back to the waterscape techniques of Suzhou's Humble Administrator's Garden — using water as paper, architecture as ink — a building philosophy common to Chinese Jiangnan gardens and waterside cities. On the opposite shore of West Lake, on Precious Stone Mountain, the game also restores the silhouette of Baochu Pagoda — this slender brick pagoda faces Leifeng Pagoda across the lake, one south, one north, one stout, one slender, forming the most classic West Lake skyline: 'Leifeng like an old monk, Baochu like a beauty.' The two pagodas, together with the Little Yingzhou islet in the lake and the pavilions and bridges along Su and Bai causeways, form the 'West Lake Architectural Culture Circle' — every one of the 'Ten Scenes of West Lake' is itself a poeticized architectural landscape. Especially worth mentioning, the game has multiple 'interactive pavilions' by the lake — enter a pavilion on the water, sit down, and the视角 automatically switches to 'scenic mode,' with erhu background music beginning. In this moment, Justice is not a game, but an immersive Song dynasty life experience.

stops.title: Stop 4: Yangzhou Gardens — The Literati Jianghu Among the Four-Season Rockeries
stops.content: As the story progresses, the player travels north from Hangzhou into Yangzhou. The Yangzhou in Justice is a city surrounded by canals and gardens. Along both banks of the canal are arcade buildings and teahouses, while in the city center lies an exquisite private garden. This garden centers on stacked rockeries, divided into four areas — spring, summer, autumn, winter — each using different types of stone:笋石, Taihu stone, yellow stone, and xuan stone. Players familiar with Chinese gardens immediately recognize this as a tribute to Yangzhou's Ge Garden. Ge Garden is one of China's four great famous gardens, the private residence of Huang Zhiyun, a salt merchant from the Two Huai region in the Qing dynasty. Its core design concept is 'Four-Season Rockeries' — using four different types of stone to分别 create the landscapes of spring, summer, autumn, and winter: spring mountains of笋石搭配翠竹, full of vitality; summer mountains of Taihu stone piled into cloud shapes, planted with ancient pines creating a sense of coolness; autumn mountains of yellow stone built high like Huangshan, with red maples evoking desolation; winter mountains of xuan stone white as residual snow, exuding a cold stillness. The entire garden uses stacked stones to tell a story of 'reincarnation' — the pinnacle of Chinese garden rockery art. The game uses these stacked rockeries as spaces for player exploration and lightness skill training — you must jump and climb among the bamboo笋 stones of spring mountain, pass through the Taihu stone caves of summer mountain, run along walls on the yellow stone cliffs of autumn mountain, and spar with opponents on the xuan stone platforms of winter mountain. This may be the only game that turns 'garden rock stacking' into a level design. Beyond Ge Garden, the interweaving of Yangzhou's waterways and gardens also strongly echoes the real Yangzhou's urban image of 'most residences are gardens, and there are more boats than carriages.' Along both banks of the game's canal, stone steps periodically extend into the water, with a few small boats moored — this is both a真实 record of Song dynasty Yangzhou's painted pleasure boats and the warmest detail of Justice as a 'life-oriented MMO.' When you find a quiet waterfront stone step in this game Yangzhou to sit on, watching the sunset dye the canal gold and red — you are not seeing a game scene, but some eternal quality from Du Mu's line 'Spring breeze十里 Yangzhou Road.'

stops.title: Stop 5: Luoyang Longmen — A Thousand Niches on Stone Walls Illuminate Past and Present
stops.content: If the previous stops were 'architecture on the ground,' then Justice's western capital Luoyang takes players into 'architecture on the cliffs' — the Longmen Grottoes. In the game's Luoyang area, on both banks of the Yi River, countless niches of various sizes are carved into the cliffs, Buddha figures large and small densely covering the entire cliff face. Most striking is the over ten-meter-tall Vairocana Buddha — full-cheeked, with beautiful eyes and a slight upturn at the corners of the mouth, that compassionate smile from a thousand years ago rendered exquisitely by the game engine. This is, of course, a digital recreation of Longmen Grottoes. Longmen is one of China's four great grottoes, with 2,345 niches, over 100,000 Buddha figures, and more than 2,800 inscriptions. From the Northern Wei to the Tang, emperors and nobles of successive dynasties接力 carved here, turning the limestone cliffs on both sides of the Yi River into the highest hall of Chinese stone carving art. Justice's recreation of Longmen features one particularly clever approach: rather than attempting to recreate the entire Longmen (which would be too large for a game), it selects the most representative Fengxian Temple Grand Buddha and several classic caves for high-precision reconstruction, then uses 'distant景 blurring' to暗示 the scale of the grotto cluster. The Vairocana Buddha of Fengxian Temple — said to have been carved in the likeness of Empress Wu Zetian — maintains in the game that sacred scale where 'standing before her, you unconsciously fall silent.' Moreover, the game adds unique exploration mechanics in the grotto area: climbing the cliffs to search for hidden 'pigeon-hole'-sized miniature niches containing rare items — this恰恰 matches a real feature of Longmen: many exquisite carvings are hidden in inconspicuous small niches, requiring careful discovery to find. More meaningfully, within the game's Luoyang city there is also a tall octagonal glazed pagoda — another digital incarnation of Youguo Temple Pagoda (Kaifeng Iron Pagoda). The Kaifeng Iron Pagoda and Longmen Grottoes — one representing the highest level of Song dynasty brick-and-stone pagoda construction, the other representing the pinnacle of stone carving art from the Northern Wei to the Tang — are connected through the game's Luoyang city, completing a 'dialogue of national treasures' across time and space. As you take a small boat along the Yi River in the game, the grottoes on both banks lit by candlelight in the night — in that moment, you are not playing an online game; you are traveling back to Luoyang in the heyday of the Tang dynasty.

stops.title: Stop 6: Yingxian Wooden Pagoda — A Thousand-Year Timber Sentinel in the Clouds
stops.content: In Justice's 'Great Song Architecture Restoration Project,' there is one structure that transcends the limits of Song territory — it lies in Yingzhou (modern Yingxian, Shanxi), within Liao territory, yet it is the undisputed pinnacle of East Asian timber architecture. This is Buddha Palace Temple Sakyamuni Pagoda, commonly known as the Yingxian Wooden Pagoda. Built in the second year of the Liao Qingning era (1056), it stands 67.31 meters tall, the oldest and tallest pure timber pavilion-style pagoda in China. What most impresses architects about the Yingxian Wooden Pagoda is its 'five visible, nine hidden' structure: from the outside, it appears to have five stories and six eaves, but inside lie four hidden levels, actually a nine-story spatial system. Each floor is composed of inner and outer rings of wooden columns, connected layer upon layer by beams and bracket sets, forming an extremely stable 'tube-in-tube' structure. The entire pagoda uses fifty-four types of bracket sets in a total of 480 clusters — each with a different form and function, earning it the nickname 'Museum of Bracket Sets.' Justice's digital team performed millimeter-level laser scanning and photogrammetry on the pagoda. In the game, players can ascend to the top of this all-wooden giant, overlooking the vast lands north of Yanmen Pass — the warm texture unique to timber and the robust proportions of Liao architecture are perfectly recreated by the game engine. Even more precious, the game's digital model preserves a备份 accurate down to every wooden tenon of this pagoda, which has already tilted from multiple earthquakes and artillery blasts — this itself is the deepest significance of the 'Great Song Architecture Restoration Project.' As you walk inside this thousand-year wooden pagoda in the game, the层层叠叠 bracket sets unfold above your head like wooden lotuses in bloom — nine hundred years ago, a Liao craftsman completed this work with chisel and axe; nine hundred years later, a Hangzhou game company uses digital technology to keep it alive forever.
